message.content:
Upgrade the Weekly AI Report feature completely.

## 1. Report UI Change
Replace the plain text card with a proper report layout:

- Header: "Weekly Nutrition Report" + date range 
  (e.g. "May 1 – May 7, 2026")
- Sections with icons:
  🌸 Overview — total avg calories, best day, worst day
  💪 Macro Summary — avg protein, carbs, fat vs goals
  📈 Highlights — what went well
  ⚠️ Areas to Improve — what needs work  
  🎯 Next Week Goal — personalized AI recommendation
- Clean card design matching pastel theme
- "Download PDF Report" button at bottom

## 2. Weekly Chart in Report
Add a bar chart inside the report using Recharts:
- X axis: days of week (Mon–Sun)
- Y axis: calories
- Bars: pastel rosé color (#e0789a)
- Show goal line as dashed horizontal line
- Below chart: mini macro table showing 
  each day's P/C/F breakdown

## 3. PDF Download
Install: npm install jspdf html2canvas

Create a downloadPDF function:

import jsPDF from 'jspdf'
import html2canvas from 'html2canvas'

const downloadPDF = async () => {
  const reportEl = document.getElementById('weekly-report')
  const canvas = await html2canvas(reportEl, { 
    scale: 2,
    backgroundColor: '#fdf6f2',
    useCORS: true
  })
  const imgData = canvas.toDataURL('image/png')
  const pdf = new jsPDF({
    orientation: 'portrait',
    unit: 'mm',
    format: 'a4'
  })
  
  const pdfWidth = pdf.internal.pageSize.getWidth()
  const pdfHeight = (canvas.height * pdfWidth) / canvas.width
  
  pdf.addImage(imgData, 'PNG', 0, 0, pdfWidth, pdfHeight)
  pdf.save(`CalSnap-Report-${new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)}.pdf`)
}

## 4. Report Content Structure
The AI generated text should be structured as JSON:

{
  "overview": "2-3 sentence overall summary",
  "bestDay": { "day": "Wednesday", "calories": 1850 },
  "worstDay": { "day": "Monday", "calories": 420 },
  "highlights": ["point 1", "point 2", "point 3"],
  "improvements": ["point 1", "point 2"],
  "nextWeekGoal": "specific personalized goal sentence",
  "macroGaps": {
    "protein": "low/good/high",
    "carbs": "low/good/high", 
    "fat": "low/good/high"
  }
}

Parse this JSON and render each section separately
in the report card with proper headings and styling.

## 5. Report Card Styling
- White background card with pastel border
- Each section has its own colored pill header
- Rosé for highlights, lavender for improvements,
  matcha for next week goal
- App logo/name "CalSnap 🌸" at top of PDF
- Footer: "Generated by CalSnap · [date]"
- Page looks professional enough to share

## 6. Download Button
- Full width button at bottom of report
- Lavender gradient background
- "⬇ Download PDF Report" text
- Loading state: "Generating PDF..."
- On success: brief "Downloaded!" confirmation

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.

27	  const [state, setState] = useState(() => {
28	    try {
29	      const saved = localStorage.getItem('calsnap_state')
30	      return saved ? { ...DEFAULT_STATE, ...JSON.parse(saved) } : DEFAULT_STATE
31	    } catch {
32	      return DEFAULT_STATE
33	    }

42	  }, [])
43	
44	  const completeOnboarding = useCallback((data) => {

46	  }, [])

48	  const addDiaryEntry = useCallback((entry) => {

52	      const newEntry = { ...entry, id: Date.now(), timestamp: new Date().toISOString() }
53	      const newDiary = { ...prev.diary, [date]: [...dayEntries, newEntry] }
54	
55	      let streak = prev.streak
56	      let lastLogDate = prev.lastLogDate
57	      const milestones = [...(prev.milestones || [])]
58	
59	      if (lastLogDate !== date) {
60	        const yesterday = new Date()
61	        yesterday.setDate(yesterday.getDate() - 1)
62	        const yStr = yesterday.toISOString().slice(0, 10)
63	        streak = lastLogDate === yStr ? streak + 1 : 1
64	        lastLogDate = date
65	        ;[3, 7, 14, 30].forEach(m => {
66	          if (streak >= m && !milestones.includes(m)) milestones.push(m)
67	        })
68	      }
69	
70	      return { ...prev, diary: newDiary, streak, lastLogDate, milestones }
71	    })
72	  }, [])
73	
74	  const deleteDiaryEntry = useCallback((id) => {
75	    const date = today()
76	    setState(prev => {
77	      const dayEntries = (prev.diary[date] || []).filter(e => e.id !== id)
78	      return { ...prev, diary: { ...prev.diary, [date]: dayEntries } }
79	    })
80	  }, [])
81	
82	  const logWater = useCallback((amount) => {
83	    const date = today()
84	    setState(prev => {
85	      const current = prev.water[date] || 0

87	    })
88	  }, [])

91	    setState(prev => ({

103	      protein: acc.protein + (e.protein || 0),
104	      carbs: acc.carbs + (e.carbs || 0),

5	export function useCalorieData() {
6	  const { diary, calorieGoal, todayEntries, todayTotals } = useUser()
7	
8	  const goals = useMemo(() => macroGoals(calorieGoal), [calorieGoal])
9	
10	  const forecast = useMemo(() => forecastCalories(todayEntries), [todayEntries])
11	
12	  const weekData = useMemo(() => {
13	    const days = []
14	    for (let i = 6; i >= 0; i--) {
15	      const d = new Date()
16	      d.setDate(d.getDate() - i)
17	      const key = d.toISOString().slice(0, 10)
18	      const label = d.toLocaleDateString('en', { weekday: 'short' })
19	      const entries = diary[key] || []
20	      const { kcal, protein, carbs, fat } = calculateMacros(entries)
21	      days.push({ date: key, label, kcal, protein, carbs, fat })
22	    }
23	    return days
24	  }, [diary])
25	
26	  const bestDay = useMemo(() => {
27	    if (!weekData.length) return null
28	    return weekData.reduce((best, d) => (d.kcal <= calorieGoal && d.kcal > (best?.kcal || 0) ? d : best), null)
29	  }, [weekData, calorieGoal])
30	
31	  const worstDay = useMemo(() => {
32	    if (!weekData.length) return null
33	    return weekData.reduce((worst, d) => (d.kcal > (worst?.kcal || 0) ? d : worst), null)
34	  }, [weekData])
35	
36	  return { todayTotals, goals, forecast, weekData, bestDay, worstDay }
37	}
